mechanism: Phenytoin can cause hypokalemia through increased renal potassium wasting and enhanced cellular uptake, while hyperkalemia increases phenytoin cardiotoxicity risk and arrhythmia potential.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly; maintain potassium within normal range (3.5-5.0 mEq/L) and assess cardiac status with ECG if potassium abnormalities develop during phenytoin therapy.
